LiteLLM release pipeline shipped Python startup malware

Target: LiteLLM · repo
Date: 2026-10-10
Target Kind: library
Language: Python
Impact: credential_theft, remote_code_execution
Phase: ci_cd

Synopsis

An attacker used stolen release credentials to publish LiteLLM 1.107.0 on October 21. Its wheels and container image carried Python startup hooks that stole secrets and loaded remote code.

Story

Secret-stealing workflows ran in the upstream repository on October 10 and 12. Later vendor findings linked a stolen GitHub token to approval of the October 21 release.

Container provenance recorded Berri-AI/litellm as its source, rather than the legitimate BerriAI organization. The malicious build included cook.pth, cook.py, and sitecustomize.py.

The installed startup hooks collected cloud and AI credentials and could execute remotely supplied Python. Floating container tags also resolved to the affected image. This incident is separate from the March LiteLLM compromise.
